summary: The mechanism (Marlin W4A16 is a small-M engine running at ~137 TFLOP/s on 1.65 TFLOP of expert work, 11-12 ms of a 17-25 ms shape; a BF16 tensor-core grouped GEMM should do it in half) is plausible and large enough that a single run is interpretable in either direction, with the per-kernel profile separating the dequant kernel, moe_align and the two fused_moe calls from the Marlin numbers already in the parity profile. The hypothesis's own arithmetic is wrong by 8x (it is ~512 rows per local expert and 8 Marlin m-blocks, not 4096 and 64) but the direction survives the correction.
justification: Profile support (parity job 62025c368c3c4e8e): Marlin takes 11995/11106/10240/10912 us on the four first-turn shapes, 44-64% of 18.3/17.0/21.5/25.3 ms, and the SoL floors are 5.5-9.8 ms. The expert work at T=16384 is 16384*8/256*32 = 16384 local (token,expert) rows x 2 x (4096*8192 + 4096*4096) = 1.65 TFLOP (this matches the hypothesis's own 1.65 TFLOP and the ctx=0 floor of 5518 us), so Marlin runs at ~137 TFLOP/s, 14% of peak. That is the real headroom. The hypothesis's stated cause is wrong: with 256 experts and random routing each local expert sees ~512 rows, not 4096, so Marlin makes ~8 passes per expert with block_size_m=64, not 64, and each expert's packed w13 (16.8 MB) fits in H200's 50 MB L2, so the re-streaming is mostly L2 traffic, not HBM. Marlin's cost is its small-M design (64-row tiles, dequant in the MMA loop, few MMA warps), which is a sound reason to expect a BF16 tensor-core engine to win at M=512/expert, just not the reason given. Budget with the corrected numbers: dequant 0.9 GB read + 3.2 GB write ~1.0-1.5 ms if the Triton dequant kernel is bandwidth-efficient; two fused_moe calls on 1.65 TFLOP at 300 TFLOP/s ~5.5 ms (weights re-read 4x per expert at BLOCK_M=128 = ~13 GB, 2.7 ms, under the compute time); total ~7 ms vs 12 ms, i.e. ~5 ms off each first-turn shape, first-turn load ~1.25x, geomean ~1.08x. Break-even needs the Triton kernels to fall below ~160 TFLOP/s, which is possible for BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=64 (SGLang's large-M BF16 configs usually use BLOCK_N=256) and with 128-row blocks on ~512-row experts the average padding waste is ~12% and up to 25%. Expected table is consistent with TASK.md: the 138-weight ctx=32768 sliding shape has the largest Marlin share (64%), so first_turn (one of three equal loads) carries the gain; turn_1/turn_4 stay on Marlin and are true controls. Weakest link: the gain rests entirely on an unmeasured assumption that SGLang's generic Triton fused_moe_kernel reaches >~200 TFLOP/s at these shapes with the hand-picked config; the sister problem (moe_w4a16) found the Triton MoE kernel 2-2.6x slower than Marlin, though at small M with in-kernel dequant, so it is a caution, not a refutation. Second: the GEMM-level numbers in the change paragraph and in the two queued dependents (threshold-turn4 says '~753 rows per local expert' for T=3012; it is ~94) propagate the same 8x error.
confounders: sglang-pipeline-parity (the base): it supplies the -1 local_ids via the Triton remap, moe_align_block_size with N_EXPERTS=256 and -1 ids, silu_and_mul(expert_ids=local_ids) and the slot-masked weighted sum that the new path reuses; the Triton fused_moe kernel relies on moe_align emitting expert_ids == -1 for the non-local blocks exactly as Marlin's is_ep path does, which is SGLang's own EP contract, so this is a dependency, not a confounder. Its own effect is below noise (all shapes 0.987-1.009x), and the only shape it moved, ctx=32768 full at 0.9865x, has err_ns 186 us from FA3 noise, far below the multi-ms effect claimed here. Nothing else has landed; nothing to revert or retune.
interference: No companion is warranted. The change has three sub-parts (per-call dequant, align at BLOCK_M=128, two Triton BF16 fused_moe calls), but the dequant can only add time and the GEMM swap is the only possible source of a gain, so the direction of any net result is unambiguous. The magnitude is attributable from the run's own profile: the dequant kernel, moe_align_block_size (block 128) and the two fused_moe_kernel calls appear as separate rows, and the parity profile already gives Marlin's 10.2-12.0 ms on the same shapes, so a loss splits cleanly into 'Triton GEMM slower than Marlin outright' versus 'GEMM faster but dequant round trip ate it' without a second run. turn_1 and turn_4 stay on the untouched Marlin path and act as built-in flat controls. The queued dependents already cover the tuning branches a companion would otherwise supply: experts-dequant-overlap-attention (hide the dequant), experts-dequant-grouped-mm-cutlass (engine swap), experts-dequant-threshold-turn4 (gate); an ab-tune on the Triton tile config (BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_M=64) is the one follow-up not yet queued, but it is only worth a run after this result shows the fused_moe rows, so it is not a companion.
rules_flags: Weights precision: a full BF16 copy of w13/w2 (3.2 GB) is materialized every call from NVFP4 inside the timed call and never stored in state; TASK.md allows 'dequantizing inside your kernels', and the copy is recomputed each replay, so this is defensible, but it is the strongest reading of that clause (the graph pool keeps the physical buffer between replays). Keep the raw NVFP4 tensors as the only weight-derived expert state and do not cache the BF16 result across calls.

The prepare() equality check must import nvfp4 (the helper the judge supplies), never reference.py or checks.py; and it should not assert bit-exact equality against nvfp4.dequantize unless the kernel multiplies in the same order ((sf*gs) first, then the E2M1 value, in fp32, then one bf16 round) — an fp32 ordering difference can flip a bf16 rounding at a tie and fail prepare() spuriously. Use the same order or a tolerance of 1 bf16 ulp.

CUDA graph: the two torch.empty calls (3.2 GB) and the moe_align buffers are sized from config/shape only, fine; make sure no .item()/host read is used to size the fused_moe grid (SGLang's invoke_fused_moe_kernel sizes it from sorted_token_ids.shape[0], which is the static padded maximum).

Activations: A operands bf16, fp32 accumulate, bf16 outputs, same as SGLang's own BF16 fused_moe path and as Marlin's W4A16; the weighted-sum and silu paths are unchanged. No change to attention, cache, routing or input-derived caching.

Memory: per captured graph the new path adds 3.2 GB (BF16 weights) to the ~3.2 GB cache13/cache2 the parity path already allocates; with 8 shapes captured in one run plus SGLang's graphs this is tens of GB on a 141 GB H200, fine, but the q_len 4096 test also takes the gated path, so it must survive on that shape too.
open_questions: invoke_fused_moe_kernel at SGLang a55ab7d expects C as [M, top_k, N] (it reads C.stride(1) and C.stride(2)) and B as [E, N, K]; pass cache1 as cache1.view(T, 8, 8192) and cache3 as cache3.view(T*8, 1, 4096), w13_bf16 [32, 8192, 4096] and w2_bf16 [32, 4096, 4096] as built. The hypothesis text says 'C=cache1 [T*8, 8192]', which will fail on stride(2) if passed 2-D; a view is a name/shape adaptation, not a math change.

Does SGLang's moe_align_block_size place the ~114688 non-local (-1) slots into blocks that the Triton kernel then zero-fills (write_zeros_to_output), or drop them? If placed, GEMM1 zero-writes ~896 blocks x 8192 bf16 (~1.9 GB, ~0.4 ms) and GEMM2 ~1 GB, a fixed cost missing from the budget; the parity Marlin path skips those blocks without writing. Check in the profile whether fused_moe_kernel time is consistent with 16384 live rows.

Rows per local expert at T=16384 is ~512 (uniform random routing over 256 experts), not 4096: correct the change paragraph's '64 passes' to '8 m-blocks' and expect ~4 m-blocks per expert at BLOCK_M=128 with ~12% average padding; the same 8x error is in experts-dequant-threshold-turn4 ('753 rows per expert' is ~94).

If the fused_moe rows come in above ~8 ms (below ~200 TFLOP/s), the tile config is the first suspect: queue an ab-tune with BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_M=64, num_stages=3 before concluding the engine loses; if they come in near 5 ms and the dequant kernel is above 2 ms, the dequant kernel is not bandwidth-efficient (byte loads, LUT gather) and experts-dequant-overlap-attention only hides it rather than fixes it.

Marlin applies the e4m3 block scale in bf16 and the global scale at the end; the single fp32 product rounded once to bf16 is at least as accurate, so the 2.5x-reference bound at q_len 4096 (the one test on the gated path, soft dist only) should pass; note the gated path is never exercised with dist=outliers.
